concept.name: Cumulative volume delta
concept.definition: The running accumulation of per-bar or per-trade volume delta over a chosen period (typically a session or an entire contract), showing the evolving net balance of aggressive buying versus aggressive selling. It summarizes who has dominated market-order flow since the chosen starting point.
concept.intuition: If delta is the score of each play, cumulative delta is the scoreboard of the whole game — it shows whether buyers or sellers have been net aggressive all session long.
concept.mechanics: Starting from zero at the session (or contract) open, each bar's delta is added to the running total; the result is plotted as bars, candles, or a line, and divergences between CVD slope and price are used analytically.
concept.formula: CVD_t = CVD_{t−1} + Delta_t, with CVD_0 = 0 at the chosen anchor (session or contract start) and Delta_t = V_ask,t − V_bid,t
concept.failure_modes: Not all markets and feeds transmit reliable trade-side data, so CVD quality varies by venue; CVD also ignores resting liquidity, so strongly positive CVD can coincide with falling prices when passive sellers absorb the flow.
concept.misconceptions: CVD is not a mechanical signal generator — platform documentation itself stresses it gives no simple buy/sell signals and must be combined with price behavior and context.
concept.example: During a session, aggressive sells push CVD steadily lower while price refuses to break a prior low; a trader reads the divergence as absorption and watches for longs rather than shorts.

citations.source: ATAS — What you should know about Cumulative Delta Analysis
